title: wk-claudemd-inline-migrate.ps1 -- MD-diet by moving single-file harness:skill locks INTO their source as inline self-guards
desc: The canonical MD-diet tool: migrates CLAUDE.md's single-file '## harness:skill <pattern>' blocks into their target source file's top as inline comment lines (source self-guards), then removes the block from CLAUDE.md. Slims CLAUDE.md with ZERO reader change and NO fail-open. Safe-by-design + fail-open-guarded + unsafe-ext-skip.
steps: WHY: CLAUDE.md bloat blocks the claude-md-diet-score gate (delegation blocked <60). The bulk is harness:skill LOCKS. You cannot remove a lock (fail-open) -- but you CAN relocate it INTO its source file as an inline header. The study-lock reader SOURCE 1 counts ANY wkappbot skill read <id> string in a file body as an inline lock, regardless of comment sigil (# or //). Proven: a .cs with 3 // wkappbot skill read lines = study-lock VALID 3/3 [inline]. So the source self-guards; CLAUDE.md loses the block; enforcement is unchanged; no fail-open (unlike an aux-manifest the reader never unions).@@RUN: ./wk-claudemd-inline-migrate.ps1 (dry-run, plan only) ; -Live (apply all safe single-file blocks) ; -Live -Max N (apply first N). Default RepoRoot = $PSScriptRoot (canonical lives at repo root).@@SAFE-BY-DESIGN (3 guards, each earned by a live bug this session 2026-07-07): (1) SINGLE-FILE ONLY -- a block migrates only if its pattern resolves to EXACTLY ONE existing repo file; 0 or 2+ (broad glob / regex-alternation / **/*.csproj) = SKIP, left in CLAUDE.md. (2) FAIL-OPEN GUARD -- a block LEAVES CLAUDE.md only if its source was ACTUALLY armed this run (or already inline); capped-by-Max / skipped blocks are RE-ADDED so they stay locked. Without this, -Max N removed all 39 blocks but armed only N sources = (39-N) UNGUARDED. (3) UNSAFE-EXT-SKIP -- only KNOWN-safe extensions get a top-of-file line comment: .cs/.ts/.js/etc => //, .ps1/.sh/.py/.md => #. XML (.csproj/.sln) and batch (.cmd/.bat) and unknown => SKIP (a # or // would break XML/batch and fail the build).@@BUG HISTORY (all found by verify-not-assume, each a lesson): (a) accumulator named $matches collided with the -match operator RESERVED automatic var $Matches (case-insensitive = same var) -> clobbered every loop -> 0 migratable. Never name a var $matches near -match. (b) the -Max fail-open above. (c) the XML/.cmd build-break above. VERIFY after any run: read a migrated source, confirm study-lock hook = VALID [inline]; then ./wkbuild.cmd green.@@RESULT 2026-07-07: migrated 35 single-file locks, CLAUDE.md 376->196 lines, build+smoke green (v7.6.129), 3 unsafe (Agent.cmd + 2 .csproj) kept. Sibling tool: wk-claudemd-switchover (shares the harness:skill block state-machine parser). Cross: [[verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static]] [[skill-lock-audit-and-auto-registration-for-critical-source-files]].

RESULT: the tool works, and the one thing it does NOT anticipate is fat-source-growth refusing the very headers it writes. WHEN: you run this to slim CLAUDE.md and the commit is refused by fat-source-growth naming several sources. HOW: run wkappbot skill read wksplit-cs-utility for that gate's terms, then stash ONLY the oversize files' header additions and commit the rest -- partial migration is safe because each block travels independently -- and BEFORE you accept that revert, grep each reverted source for wkappbot skill read to confirm it still carries an inline lock, since the tool has already removed its block from CLAUDE.md and a reverted header with no pre-existing inline lock leaves that file UNGUARDED. WHY: measured 2026-08-28 in WKAppBot on an owner directive to move CLAUDE.md content into skills. Plan found 20 migratable blocks; -Max 1 proved the fail-open guard live by arming one source and deliberately keeping the other 19 blocks; the full run moved 18 and skipped 2 unsafe extensions, taking CLAUDE.md from 549 lines and 52,910 bytes to 451 and 41,754. Then the commit was refused: bin/wksplit-cs.py at 1006 lines, bin/wktest-smoke.sh at 441, RunCommand.Pty.cs at 711 and SlackCommands.cs at 1508 were each being grown by 5 to 8 comment lines. THE TWO GUARDS GENUINELY DISAGREE -- this tool's whole design is to put locks INTO source headers, and that gate exists to stop source files growing -- so a fat file can never receive its lock this way and its block must stay in CLAUDE.md. THE NEAR-MISS WORTH KEEPING: after stashing those four, two of them showed ZERO occurrences of their own name in CLAUDE.md, which looked like a fail-open I had just created; grepping the sources showed both already carried inline locks of their own, 5 and 3 lines, so nothing was actually unguarded. Check the SOURCE before concluding a lock is lost -- the absence of a CLAUDE.md block is only half the picture.

BUG: a file that is DEPLOYED OR REGENERATED from an upstream master is not a valid inline-lock target, and this tool cannot tell from the path. WHEN: choosing which blocks to migrate, or explaining why a migrated header vanished. HOW: run wkappbot skill read ask-health-check-ref for the install-master mechanism, then before accepting any migration ask whether the file has an UPSTREAM COPY that a deploy writes over -- if it does, leave its block in CLAUDE.md; the extension being safe is not sufficient. VERIFY afterwards with git diff on the migrated file a few minutes later, because the overwrite is silent and the file simply reads as though you never edited it. WHY: measured 2026-08-28. bin/wkask.sh took its three skill-read lines cleanly, and they were gone twice -- the second time within seconds of a stash restoring them. That file's own history records the cause: the corrupted copy IS the install master, held in wkappbot-kih and personal-docs, and a deploy copies it back over every local edit, which is how it has been reverted at least eleven times. THE DANGER IS ASYMMETRIC AND SILENT: the tool had already removed the block from CLAUDE.md, so had CLAUDE.md not still carried three other wkask references the file would have been left guarded by NOTHING -- lock deleted from the manifest, header erased by the next deploy, and no error anywhere. Reverted and committed as 4f743ee7ed with the block kept in CLAUDE.md, which is the correct home for this one file rather than a compromise.

RESULT: the .cmd skip is OVER-CAUTIOUS and costs two blocks -- batch files support REM, so the unsafe-extension list can admit them. WHEN: you run this tool and see 'SKIP (unsafe comment syntax -- XML/batch/unknown ext)' naming a .cmd or .bat, or you are extending the extension map in the tool itself. HOW: run wkappbot skill read verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static-howto for the run-it-do-not-read-it discipline, then map .cmd and .bat to the REM sigil rather than skipping them, and prove it the way batch actually fails -- execute the file afterwards, since a broken batch line does not error at parse time, it silently changes control flow. Leave .csproj and .sln skipped; XML genuinely has no line-comment form and that half of the guard is correct. WHY: measured 2026-09-03 in WKAppBot. A -Live run found 6 migratable blocks, moved 4, and skipped bin/wk-splice-to-live.cmd and bin/Agent.cmd on extension alone. Earlier in the same session I had added TWELVE REM lines to the head of bin/wk-gitsync-probe.cmd, committed as e5bb8439d4, and the launcher still runs -- so the evidence that batch tolerates leading REM was already sitting in this repo when the tool refused to use it. THE SHAPE WORTH KEEPING: the guard's three protections were each earned by a live bug, which makes the whole list feel proven, but only the XML half of the third one was ever tested -- an extension bundled into a skip-list by association inherits a caution nobody measured for it. Check which members of a safety list have their own evidence before treating the list as settled.

INCIDENT: admitting .cmd with REM was CORRECT in syntax and WRONG in effect -- the sigil is not the whole safety question, ECHO SUPPRESSION is. WHEN: extending the extension-to-sigil map to batch, or reviewing the .cmd arm that now exists in Get-CommentPrefix. HOW: run wkappbot skill read verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static-howto, then before migrating any batch file check that it BEGINS with an echo-suppressing line and that the header would land AFTER it -- and prove it by EXECUTING the migrated file, never by reading it, because a batch file with a legal-but-misplaced line does not error, it just behaves differently. WHY: measured 2026-09-03 in WKAppBot, and I reverted my own change. I promoted the .cmd arm, ran -Live, and the two migrated files took their REM headers cleanly. Then running bin/Agent.cmd printed all four header lines to the console on every invocation, because Agent.cmd has no @echo off at all and wk-splice-to-live.cmd puts its @echo off AFTER where the header lands. Worse, batch EXPANDED the %* inside one REM line into the actual arguments, so the comment text a reader sees at runtime is not the comment that was written. Agent.cmd is this repo's delegation front door and is called constantly; trading its observable output for ten lines of CLAUDE.md is a bad exchange, so both migrations were reverted with git checkout HEAD on the named paths and Agent.cmd verified clean by re-running it. THE RULE THAT GENERALISES: an extension's comment SIGIL tells you the line will parse; it tells you nothing about whether the file will still behave the same. Keep .cmd and .bat OUT of the migratable set until the tool can place the header after an echo-suppressing prologue, and treat my earlier step here -- which called the skip merely over-cautious -- as half right: the skip was over-cautious about SYNTAX and correct about EFFECT.

requirements.expect: prints migratable single-file blocks count + dry-run plan
arms exactly 1 source, removes exactly 1 block from CLAUDE.md (fail-open guard: 38 kept)
